chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yaf'ur, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to him, 'How was Friday named?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered His creation in it for the Wilayah of Muhammad and his successor regarding the Covenant. Thus, He named it the day of Friday (Jumu'ah) due to the gathering (Jama'ah) of His creation in it.'

key_terms.الْجَمْعُ: Gathering, referring to the collection of creation
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةُ: Friday, derived from the root meaning 'gathering'
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقُ: The primordial Covenant of the souls
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: Guardianship or authority, specifically referring to the divine authority of the Prophet and Imams

ai.seo_question: Why is the day of Friday called Jumu'ah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the name 'Friday' (Jumu'ah) derives from the Arabic root for 'gathering,' signifying that Allah gathered the souls of His creation on this day to affirm the Wilayah of Prophet Muhammad and his successor within the primordial Covenant (Mithaq). This etymological link underscores the day's theological centrality in Shia tradition, where Friday serves not merely as a weekly congregational prayer but as the annual commemoration of the cosmic gathering of believers to the light of the Ahl al-Bayt.
